authority.geography_type: a large drowned-valley harbour (Port Jackson) with a tidal river arm (Parramatta River) and ocean-facing approaches
authority.home_waters_label: Sydney Harbour and the Parramatta River

mandate.summary: Transport for NSW plans, contracts and regulates all public transport in New South Wales — trains, metro, light rail, buses and the Sydney Ferries network. Ferries are an integrated Opal-fare public mode across Sydney Harbour and the Parramatta River, operated under contract on the F1-F10 routes.
current_priorities: Run and grow the Sydney Ferries network (F1-F10) as an integrated Opal public mode
Deliver Future Transport / NSW net-zero by 2050 with a zero-emission public fleet
Trial and roll out electric ferries - the first NSW electric ferry is due on the new Sydney Fish Market service from 2029
Add wharves and services as the harbour-front and river corridors densify

policy_targets.vision: Future Transport Strategy; NSW net-zero by 2050; zero-emission public transport fleet
policy_targets.decarb_note: NSW has committed to a zero-emission transport fleet; the first NSW electric ferry is planned for the new Sydney Fish Market route from 2029.
policy_targets.relevance: A zero-emission foiling tier is exactly the fleet renewal the net-zero mandate requires - faster and quieter than the current RiverCat/Emerald displacement fleet, and able to open low-wake river and cross-harbour lines.

precedent.headline: Sydney already runs one of the world's iconic public ferry networks - ten routes, ~38 wharves, Opal-integrated.
precedent.network: F1 Manly, F2 Taronga Zoo, F3 Parramatta River, F4 Pyrmont Bay, F5 Neutral Bay, F6 Mosman Bay, F7 Double Bay, F8 Cockatoo Island, F9 Watsons Bay, F10 Blackwattle Bay - operated under contract, fully on Opal fares.
precedent.note: Ferries are a mainstream, everyday public mode in Sydney, not a novelty. The opportunity is to renew and decarbonize the fleet and add high-value low-wake lines.

interpretation_for_navier: Navier is the software-defined, zero-emission foiling upgrade to a public ferry mode Sydney already runs at scale. Foiling hulls are faster, near-silent and low-wake - ideal for the wake-sensitive Parramatta River and for fast cross-harbour hops - while the heritage Manly and inner-harbour services continue underneath.

domestic_network.note: Candidate boarding points with APPROXIMATE anchor coordinates [lng, lat] for Grok to snap to real piers/wharves/terminals during seal. Coordinates are anchors, not sealed geometry. Core mirrors the authority's live public-ferry stops; new/committed stops are flagged.

boarding_points.name: Sydney Fish Market Wharf (new, electric ferry 2029)

domestic_pairs.rationale: The iconic F1 - Circular Quay to Manly across the harbour; a fast, low-noise foiling upgrade on Sydney's busiest ferry line.
Short high-frequency CBD hop between Circular Quay and Barangaroo.
Eastern-harbour run to Watsons Bay via Rose Bay; bypasses the New South Head Road corridor.
The full Parramatta River corridor (displacement / no-foil on the upper river) linking the CBD to Parramatta's second CBD.
North-shore cove service to Mosman Bay; quiet, low-wake foiling between the headlands.
Inner-harbour heritage-island line via Balmain and Birchgrove.
Short Blackwattle/Pyrmont line serving the new Sydney Fish Market - the first NSW electric-ferry corridor, foiling-ready.
Cross-harbour hop to Taronga Zoo; high-demand, wake-sensitive.

regional_links.note: Sydney Ferries is an inner-harbour and river network; there is no domestic long-range marine corridor in scope. Ocean services beyond the Heads (e.g. toward the Central Coast / Pittwater) are a far-future roadmap item only and not part of the core proposal.

routing_hazards.instruction: Every domestic and regional leg must be routed through navigable open water with NO land crossings (interior_land_km == 0). Hand-curated waypoints required wherever a breakwater, barrier, bridge pier, reef, headland, naval zone or shallows would otherwise be clipped.

hazards.detail: The F1 Manly run crosses the open Heads where harbour meets the Pacific - exposed to ocean swell. Route through the marked harbour channel; the foiling control system must manage swell and the Sow and Pigs reef off Watsons Bay.
Shallow reef in the middle of the harbour off Watsons Bay/Vaucluse - marked by beacons; hand-waypoint clear of it.

Above Gladesville the river is shallow, tidal and crossed by the Gladesville, Silverwater and other low bridges; upper-river legs must be displacement / no-foil on the dredged channel with strict wake limits past moorings and mangroves.
Garden Island (Fleet Base East) is an active RAN naval base with an exclusion zone; route clear of the restricted waters off Potts Point.
Sydney Harbour carries heavy ferry, tripboat and recreational traffic; geofence no-foil, low-wake zones at all wharf approaches and in the heritage coves.
Any Middle Harbour extension passes the Spit Bridge (a lifting bridge) - must follow the opening schedule and marked channel.
